1.visual: A browser window outline with a rounded-rectangle frame, a horizontal title bar at the top containing two small squares (representing window controls or tabs), and a large empty content area below.
1.usage: Representing a web browser or app window; opening a new browser tab; linking to a web-based resource; indicating a preview or iframe embed.

2.visual: A command symbol (the looped square or 'bowen knot' shape) composed of four rounded squares connected at their corners by curved loops, commonly associated with the macOS Command key.
2.usage: Displaying keyboard shortcut hints; macOS-specific hotkey documentation; shortcut reference panels; command palette triggers.

3.visual: A rounded rectangle divided horizontally into two sections: a large upper area and a thinner horizontal bar fixed to the bottom edge, resembling a panel with a bottom toolbar or shelf.
3.usage: Toggling a bottom panel or drawer; representing a layout with a fixed footer bar; showing a bottom navigation bar; activating a status bar.

4.visual: A rounded rectangle divided horizontally into two sections — a large upper area and a thinner bottom bar — with a checkmark icon centered in the upper area, indicating a confirmed or collapsed bottom panel state.
4.usage: Confirming closure of a bottom panel; marking a panel as resolved or done; toggling a verified bottom-shelf state; indicating a completed drawer action.

5.visual: A rounded rectangle divided horizontally into two sections — a large upper area and a thinner bottom bar — with an upward-pointing chevron centered in the upper area, suggesting the bottom panel can be collapsed or scrolled up.
5.usage: Collapsing a bottom drawer or panel upward; dismissing a bottom sheet; scrolling to the top of a panel; hiding a bottom toolbar.

6.visual: A rounded rectangle divided vertically into two unequal columns: a narrow left sidebar panel and a wider right content area, with both separated by a single vertical line.
6.usage: Toggling a left sidebar layout; switching to a two-column view with a narrow left panel; activating a navigation rail or side menu; representing a sidebar-open state.

7.visual: A rounded rectangle divided vertically into a narrow left panel and a wider right content area, with a left-pointing chevron centered inside the narrow left panel, suggesting the sidebar can be collapsed to the left.
7.usage: Collapsing a left sidebar or navigation panel; hiding a left drawer; closing a side menu; minimizing a left-side panel.

8.visual: A rounded rectangle divided vertically into a narrow left panel and a wider right content area, with a right-pointing chevron centered inside the narrow left panel, suggesting the sidebar can be expanded to the right.
8.usage: Expanding a collapsed left sidebar; opening a side navigation panel; revealing a hidden left drawer; showing a side menu.

9.visual: A rounded rectangle divided vertically into a wider left content area and a narrow right panel, with both separated by a single vertical line — the mirror image of the left-sidebar layout icon.
9.usage: Toggling a right sidebar or details panel; switching to a two-column view with a narrow right panel; activating a properties or inspector panel on the right; representing a right-side panel open state.

10.visual: A rounded rectangle divided vertically into a wider left content area and a narrow right panel, with a right-pointing chevron centered inside the narrow right panel, suggesting the right sidebar can be collapsed outward.
10.usage: Collapsing a right sidebar or details panel; hiding a right drawer; closing a properties inspector; minimizing a right-side panel.

11.visual: A rounded rectangle divided vertically into a wider left content area and a narrow right panel, with a left-pointing chevron centered inside the narrow right panel, suggesting the right sidebar can be expanded inward.
11.usage: Expanding a collapsed right sidebar; opening a right-side details or inspector panel; revealing a hidden right drawer; showing contextual properties.

12.visual: A power symbol: a circle with a gap at the top center and a short vertical line extending upward through the gap, universally recognized as a power on/off button icon.
12.usage: Power on/off controls; shutting down or restarting a system; sleep or standby toggles; device or session termination actions.

13.visual: Two stacked chevrons pointing in opposite vertical directions (one up, one down) with a horizontal line between them, forming a sort or resize handle indicator.
13.usage: Sorting a table column in either direction; indicating a draggable resize handle; representing a toggle between ascending and descending order; showing an expandable/collapsible row splitter.
